- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp spikes; cap upward revisions.
- After a price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a mild upward bias to prevent premature mean reversion.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect earlier trend reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a downward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility or mixed signals, reduce forecast variance; avoid large swings in 30-day predictions.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model may overfit recent momentum; dampen forecast growth rate slightly.
